#### Initial Analysis of Response Variable {#sec-ppc-512}

[**Initial Plots of Response Variable**]{#sec-ppc-512-plots}

The initial step is to assess data quality and to look for anomalies. This is done by generating a [normal probability plot](../01-eda/index.qmd#sec-eda-normal-probability-plot), a [histogram](../01-eda/index.qmd#sec-eda-histogram), and a [box plot](../01-eda/index.qmd#sec-eda-box-plot). For convenience, these are generated on a single page.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| message: false
#| label: fig-ppc-512-initial-plots
#| fig-cap: "Normal probability plot, box plot, and histogram of film thickness"
library(patchwork)

p_qq <- ggplot(furnace, aes(sample = thickness)) +
  stat_qq(color = "steelblue") +
  stat_qq_line(color = "firebrick") +
  labs(x = "Theoretical Quantiles", y = "Thickness (Å)", title = "Normal Probability Plot") +
  theme_light()

p_box <- ggplot(furnace, aes(y = thickness, x = "")) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.5) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Thickness (Å)", title = "Box Plot") +
  theme_light()

p_hist <- ggplot(furnace, aes(thickness)) +
  geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), bins = 15, fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.6, color = "white") +
  stat_function(fun = dnorm, args = list(mean = mean(furnace$thickness), sd = sd(furnace$thickness)), color = "firebrick", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = "Thickness (Å)", y = "Density", title = "Histogram") +
  theme_light()

p_qq + p_box + p_hist
```

[**Conclusions From the Plots**]{#sec-ppc-512-conclusions-plots}

We can make the following conclusions based on these initial plots.

- The box plot indicates one outlier. However, this outlier is only slightly smaller than the other numbers.
- The normal probability plot and the histogram (with an overlaid normal density) indicate that this data set is reasonably approximated by a normal distribution.

[**Parameter Estimates**]{#sec-ppc-512-parameter-estimates}

Parameter estimates for the film thickness are summarized in the following table.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
mnt <- mean(furnace$thickness)
sdt <- sd(furnace$thickness)
n <- nrow(furnace)
stderr <- sdt / sqrt(n)
dof <- n - 1
alpha <- 0.05
Tvalue <- qt(1 - alpha / 2, df = dof)

tibble(
  Type = c("Location", "Dispersion"),
  Parameter = c("Mean", "Standard Deviation"),
  Estimate = c(mnt, sdt),
  `Lower (95%) CI` = c(mnt - Tvalue * stderr, sdt * sqrt(dof / qchisq(1 - alpha / 2, dof))),
  `Upper (95%) CI` = c(mnt + Tvalue * stderr, sdt * sqrt(dof / qchisq(alpha / 2, dof)))
)
```

[**Quantiles**]{#sec-ppc-512-quantiles}

Quantiles for the film thickness are summarized in the following table.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
p <- c(0, 0.5, 2.5, 10, 25, 50, 75, 90, 95, 97.5, 99.5, 100) / 100
tibble(
  Percentile = scales::percent(p),
  Quantile = round(quantile(furnace$thickness, probs = p, type = 6), 2)
)
```

[**Capability Analysis**]{#sec-ppc-512-capability}

From the above preliminary analysis, it looks reasonable to proceed with the [capability analysis](#sec-ppc-46). The lower specification limit is 460, the upper specification limit is 660, and the target specification is 560.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
#| label: fig-ppc-512-capability
#| fig-cap: "Histogram of film thickness with specification limits (LSL = 460, USL = 660, target = 560)"
LSL <- 460
USL <- 660
Target <- 560

ggplot(furnace, aes(thickness)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 15, fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.6, color = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(LSL, USL), color = "firebrick", linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = Target, color = "grey40", linetype = "dotted") +
  labs(x = "Thickness (Å)", y = "Count") +
  theme_light()
```

[**Percent Defective**]{#sec-ppc-512-percent-defective}

We summarize the percent defective (i.e., the number of items outside the specification limits) in the following table.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
defect_act_lt <- 100 * sum(furnace$thickness < LSL) / n
defect_act_gt <- 100 * sum(furnace$thickness > USL) / n
defect_act_total <- 100 * sum(furnace$thickness < LSL | furnace$thickness > USL) / n

defect_theo_lt <- 100 * pnorm((LSL - mnt) / sdt)
defect_theo_gt <- 100 * pnorm((USL - mnt) / sdt, lower.tail = FALSE)
defect_theo_total <- defect_theo_lt + defect_theo_gt

tibble(
  Specification = c("Lower Specification Limit", "Upper Specification Limit", "Specification Target"),
  Value = c(LSL, USL, Target),
  `% Actual` = round(c(defect_act_lt, defect_act_gt, defect_act_total), 4),
  `% Theoretical` = round(c(defect_theo_lt, defect_theo_gt, defect_theo_total), 5)
)
```

The percent below LSL is $100\Phi\left(\frac{\text{LSL} - \bar{y}}{s}\right)$ and the percent above USL is $100\Phi\left(\frac{\text{USL} - \bar{y}}{s}\right)$, where $\Phi$ denotes the normal cumulative distribution function, $\bar{y}$ the sample mean, and $s$ the sample standard deviation.

[**Capability Index Statistics**]{#sec-ppc-512-capability-indices}

We summarize various capability index statistics in the following table.

```{r}
#| code-fold: true
Cpi <- (USL - LSL) / (6 * sdt)
Cp_cilo <- Cpi * sqrt(qchisq(alpha / 2, dof) / dof)
Cp_ciup <- Cpi * sqrt(qchisq(1 - alpha / 2, dof) / dof)

CpLi <- (mnt - LSL) / (3 * sdt)
CpL_se <- sqrt(1 / (9 * n) + (CpLi^2) / (2 * dof))
CpL_cilo <- CpLi - qnorm(1 - alpha / 2) * CpL_se
CpL_ciup <- CpLi + qnorm(1 - alpha / 2) * CpL_se

CpUi <- (USL - mnt) / (3 * sdt)
CpU_se <- sqrt(1 / (9 * n) + (CpUi^2) / (2 * dof))
CpU_cilo <- CpUi - qnorm(1 - alpha / 2) * CpU_se
CpU_ciup <- CpUi + qnorm(1 - alpha / 2) * CpU_se

Cpki <- min(CpLi, CpUi)
Cpk_se <- sqrt(1 / (9 * n) + (Cpki^2) / (2 * dof))
Cpk_cilo <- Cpki - qnorm(1 - alpha / 2) * Cpk_se
Cpk_ciup <- Cpki + qnorm(1 - alpha / 2) * Cpk_se

Cpmi <- (USL - LSL) / (6 * sqrt(sdt^2 + (mnt - Target)^2))
Cpm_cilo <- Cpmi * sqrt(qchisq(alpha / 2, dof) / dof)
Cpm_ciup <- Cpmi * sqrt(qchisq(1 - alpha / 2, dof) / dof)

tibble(
  `Capability Statistic` = c("Cp", "CpL", "CpU", "Cpk", "Cpm"),
  Index = round(c(Cpi, CpLi, CpUi, Cpki, Cpmi), 3),
  `Lower CI` = round(c(Cp_cilo, CpL_cilo, CpU_cilo, Cpk_cilo, Cpm_cilo), 3),
  `Upper CI` = round(c(Cp_ciup, CpL_ciup, CpU_ciup, Cpk_ciup, Cpm_ciup), 3)
)
```

[**Conclusions**]{#sec-ppc-512-conclusions}

The above capability analysis indicates that the process is capable and we can proceed with the analysis.
